title: Synthesis --- The Thing and the Person

lessons.title: Synthesis — the thing and the person, in one sentence
lessons.gloss: synthesis — choosing between the two sets at conversation speed, where the choice is made by meaning and not by a table

segments.text: Two pronouns, one question. Lo or le — what decides?
Read this aloud and watch the two sets take turns.
— ¿Tienes el libro? — Sí, lo tengo. — ¿Y Ana? — Le digo hoy.
Four turns. The book gets lo, because the having lands on it. Ana gets le, because the telling is aimed at her.
Nothing in the sentence shape tells you which. Same slot, two letters each, one Latin ancestor. The only thing separating them is what you mean.
That is new. Every choice so far could be settled by looking at something — a noun's ending, its article, where the stress falls. This one cannot.
In a real conversation you do not have time to run a test. So do not aim for the test — aim for the feeling of the two verbs:
Verbs that hold, make, want, see land on a thing. Those take lo, la, los, las.
Verbs that tell, speak, give, ask are aimed at a person. Those take le, les.
Say enough sentences and the verb starts arriving with its pronoun attached, which is what fluency here actually is. The test is scaffolding for when you are unsure, not the method.
And when you get it wrong you will be understood: lo digo and le digo are both ordinary sentences. You will have said something slightly other than you meant, and the person will ask.

segments.instruction: "lo tengo, le digo, los tengo, les hablo" until each verb brings its own pronoun
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "lo tengo, le digo, los tengo, les hablo" until each verb brings its own pronoun]

segments.prompt: Answer yes to Tienes el libro, without the noun.

feedback.correct: The having lands on the book.

feedback.incorrect: Les hablo — aimed at more than one person.

segments.prompt: Two pronouns in the same slot, both two letters, both from one Latin word. What is the only thing that tells them apart?
acceptedResponses: whether the verb acts on it or aims at it

feedback.correct: The first choice in this book that nothing on the page can settle.
feedback.incorrect: What you mean — whether the verb acts on the thing or is aimed at the person.

segments.text: ¿Tienes el libro? (Sí, lo tengo.) "I tell her today"? (Le digo hoy.) What decides between lo and le? (What you mean — nothing on the page.) Next: what happens when a sentence needs both at once.
